domain_label: US Fashion/Costume Jewelry — Consumer Segmentation as a Research Method (Age, Gender, Culture, Income, Occasion) and Prevalence x Frequency Sizing
purpose: A method for segmenting the US buyer of fashion/costume plated jewelry along age cohort (Gen Z / 18-25 focus), gender skew, cultural/ethnic market, income and occasion/gifting cuts by pulling each cut from the correct public dataset (US Census/ACS/PUMS for population base rates, BLS Consumer Expenditure Survey for expenditure propensity, platform audience insights for reach composition), sizing 'how many buy' bottom-up via population x prevalence x frequency x spend [METHOD], and never fabricating a demographic, ethnicity, or purchase-rate number - every claim carried as [FACT] with basis, [ESTIMATE] with method+confidence, [METHOD], or [UNKNOWN], with an explicit anti-stereotyping guardrail on the cultural/ethnic cut.
assumptions: no primary market dataset is supplied; every segmentation number is either a cited public-data pull ([FACT] with source), a bottom-up [ESTIMATE] with stated method+confidence, a [METHOD] recipe to obtain it, or an honest [UNKNOWN] - the owner's 'how many / which ethnicity / which % buy' questions are answered by method, never by a guess

the US Census / American Community Survey (ACS) and its public-use microdata (PUMS) supply population base rates (age x sex x race/ethnicity x household income by geography) and are the DENOMINATOR only - they carry no jewelry-purchase behaviour [FACT-Census scope]

the BLS Consumer Expenditure Survey (CE) is the least-bad public proxy for who spends on jewelry: it reports average annual apparel-and-services / 'jewelry and watches' expenditure cross-tabbed by age-of-reference-person, income quintile, and some demographic cuts, from a national probability sample, with published standard errors [FACT-BLS CE scope]

platform audience insights (Meta/TikTok ad-manager reach + audience composition) measure ENGAGEMENT and reachable-audience size, not purchase; they carry self-selection and platform-composition bias and are a targeting proxy, not a demand measurement [FACT-platform tool scope]
the owner's 'mostly girls 18-25' is a testable HYPOTHESIS to be checked against CE, platform composition and the owner's own store data - it is a prior to test, not an established fact

cultural/ethnic-market segmentation is done as an ethics-bound research method: Census gives population base rates and observable occasion behaviour can be studied, but per-ethnicity purchase RATES are never invented and the ecological fallacy (group average != individual) is respected throughout
exclusions: category demand structure and finish/tier segmentation (earrings/necklaces/rings; solid-vs-plated share) - that is kb1_category_and_finish_demand; this KB segments the BUYER, not the product
trend signals and the brand/price-tier competitive landscape - that is kb3_trend_and_competitor_mapping

the poll/survey INSTRUMENT design, incentive/sampling bias mechanics and paid-reach mechanics - those are the jewel_poll specialist (S4); this KB only names WHO to sample and hands the segment frame across
the final ranked 6-SKU launch set and keep/cut protocol - that is the jewel_assortment specialist (S5)

asserting any actual market-size dollar figure, unit-count, per-ethnicity purchase rate, gender split percentage, or competitor share as measured fact; this KB produces the METHOD and the tagged bands, not the numbers themselves

competency_questions.question: What is the segmentation objective and unit of analysis, and why is segmentation treated as a research method rather than a demographic verdict about who 'should' buy?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SEGMENTATION_FRAME defines the unit as the US buyer of fashion/costume plated jewelry, states that segmentation exists to steer assortment/poll-targeting/ad-audience decisions, and frames every cut as a testable hypothesis carrying a tag, not an asserted fact

competency_questions.question: How is every demographic and purchase-rate claim tagged so that no market number is ever invented, and how is that discipline audited at the end?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: HONESTY_TAGGING_PROTOCOL fixes the [FACT]/[ESTIMATE]/[METHOD]/[UNKNOWN] scheme with a basis requirement, and SIZING_HONESTY_LEDGER separates dataset [FACT]s from [ESTIMATE] bands and [UNKNOWN] purchase rates in the output

competency_questions.question: Which public datasets inform each segmentation cut, and what can and cannot each one legitimately tell you?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PUBLIC_DATASET_MAP catalogs Census/ACS, BLS CE, and platform insights with each one's scope and lag/bias, CENSUS_ACS_METHOD establishes it as population denominator only, and BLS_CE_METHOD establishes it as the expenditure-propensity proxy with its standard errors

competency_questions.question: How do you size the Gen Z / 18-25 age cohort and estimate its jewelry propensity from public data without inventing a purchase rate?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: AGE_COHORT_CUT sizes the 18-25 population from Census/ACS and reads jewelry-expenditure propensity from BLS CE by age-of-reference-person, flagging the reference-person caveat and tagging the propensity an [ESTIMATE]

competency_questions.question: How do you test the owner's 'mostly girls' gender-skew hypothesis rather than assuming it?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: GENDER_SKEW_CUT treats 'mostly women 18-25' as a prior to test against CE, platform audience composition and store data, states the limits of gender data in CE, and never hardcodes the skew as a fact

competency_questions.question: How do you segment by cultural/ethnic market as a legitimate research method without stereotyping or inventing per-ethnicity purchase rates?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ETHNIC_CULTURAL_SEGMENTATION uses Census race/ethnicity for population base rates and studies observable occasion behaviour, while STEREOTYPE_GUARDRAIL binds it with the ecological-fallacy caveat, the no-invented-rate rule and the ad-policy limits on protected-class targeting

competency_questions.question: How does income segmentation align the buyer to the fashion/costume (accessible-price) tier?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: INCOME_CUT reads CE jewelry expenditure by income quintile/decile against Census household-income distribution, and links willingness-to-pay bands to the accessible fashion/costume price tier as a [METHOD], not a set price

competency_questions.question: How do you separate self-purchase demand from occasion/gifting demand, and which public signals reveal it?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: OCCASION_GIFTING_CUT distinguishes self-purchase vs gift occasions (Valentine's, Mother's Day, holidays, weddings, birthdays), reads CE seasonal/expenditure patterns and the retail calendar, and tags self-gifting as an [ESTIMATE] behaviour to test

competency_questions.question: How do you size 'how many people buy' via prevalence x frequency without fabricating a market-size number?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PREVALENCE_FREQUENCY_SIZING states buyers = population (Census) x prevalence (share who buy, from CE participation or survey) x frequency (purchases/yr) x avg spend, with every factor tagged and the output delivered as a band with a stated confidence, never a single asserted figure

competency_questions.question: How do platform audience insights proxy a segment, and why is engagement not the same as purchase?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PLATFORM_AUDIENCE_INSIGHTS reads Meta/TikTok reach and audience composition as a targeting proxy, and SELF_SELECTION_BIAS explains how self-selected, platform-skewed engagement distorts any segment estimate drawn from it

competency_questions.question: How do you triangulate several imperfect sources plus the owner's own running-store data into one honest segment profile?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SEGMENT_TRIANGULATION combines CE, Census, platform and first-party store data into a confidence-weighted segment profile, and EXISTING_STORE_DATA is used as the strongest-but-small first-party signal 'mindful of the old stuff' with its sample and privacy caveats

competency_questions.question: What does the segmentation work hand off to the poll and assortment specialists, and what stays out of scope?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SEGMENT_PRIORITIZATION ranks the actionable segments, SEGMENT_PERSONA_OUTPUT composes tagged primary/secondary personas without invented percentages, and HANDOFF_TO_POLL_ASSORTMENT passes the target frame and sizing band to S4/S5 while stopping before instrument design and SKU selection

glossary.definition: The research method of partitioning a market's buyers into groups along cuts (age, gender, culture/ethnicity, income, occasion) that differ in a decision-relevant way, done here to steer assortment, poll-targeting and ad-audience choices; each cut is a testable hypothesis carrying a [FACT]/[ESTIMATE]/[METHOD]/[UNKNOWN] tag, not an asserted demographic verdict.

A bottom-up market-sizing method: buyers/spend = population (Census base) x prevalence (share of that population who buy the category, from CE participation or a survey) x purchase frequency (times/yr) x average spend/purchase; each factor is separately sourced and tagged, and the product is reported as a band with a confidence, never as one asserted market-size number [METHOD].

The US Bureau of Labor Statistics national probability-sample survey of household spending; it reports average annual expenditure on categories including 'jewelry and watches' cross-tabbed by age-of-reference-person, income quintile and some demographic cuts, with published standard errors - the least-bad public proxy for who spends on jewelry, tagged [FACT-BLS CE] for the dataset and [ESTIMATE] for any propensity read from it.

The US Census, American Community Survey and Public-Use Microdata Sample provide population base rates (counts by age x sex x race/ethnicity x household income x geography); they are the DENOMINATOR for sizing and carry NO jewelry-purchase behaviour, so they set 'how many people exist in a cut', never 'how many buy' [FACT-Census scope].

Meta and TikTok ad-manager audience-size and composition estimates plus organic audience analytics; they measure reachable-audience size and engagement, not purchase, and carry self-selection and platform-composition bias, so they are a targeting/reach proxy tagged [ESTIMATE, platform-biased], not a demand measurement.

The rule that a group average (e.g. a cultural cohort's population base rate or observed occasion behaviour) must never be read as an individual's traits or a fabricated per-group purchase rate; cultural/ethnic segmentation is bounded by this fallacy, by the no-invented-rate honesty rule, and by ad-platform limits on protected-class targeting [FACT-method ethics].

Segmenting demand by the buying occasion - self-purchase vs gift (Valentine's, Mother's Day, winter holidays, weddings, birthdays, graduations) - read from CE seasonal expenditure patterns and the retail calendar; captures that the same person buys differently by occasion, and flags self-gifting among young women as an [ESTIMATE] behaviour to test, not a measured share.

The distortion that arises when the people who engage with, follow, or answer a survey/poll/ad are not representative of the target population; it inflates whatever the engaged group over-represents, so any segment estimate from platform insights, a poll, or store data must be discounted for it and never read as a population rate.

Combining several individually-imperfect sources (Census denominator + CE propensity + platform composition + first-party store data) into one confidence-weighted segment profile, letting agreement raise confidence and disagreement flag an [UNKNOWN], so the profile is honest about its evidence rather than resting on one fabricated figure.

The mandatory honesty scheme: [FACT] = a cited public-data or regulatory truth with basis; [ESTIMATE] = a derived number with its method and confidence; [METHOD] = a recipe to obtain a number not yet pulled; [UNKNOWN] = an honest gap; no demographic, ethnicity, gender-split or purchase-rate number ever appears untagged or as an invented fact.

nodes.definition: Fix the frame for the whole KB: the unit of analysis is the US buyer of fashion/costume plated jewelry (accessible-price gold-plated / vermeil / rhodium-plated-silver pieces), and segmentation exists to make three downstream decisions better - which segment to weight in the launch assortment, whom to target in the IG/TikTok poll, and which ad audience to buy. Every cut (age, gender, culture/ethnicity, income, occasion) is framed as a testable HYPOTHESIS that must carry a [FACT]/[ESTIMATE]/[METHOD]/[UNKNOWN] tag, never an asserted demographic verdict about who 'should' buy [METHOD]. The frame explicitly rejects the pattern of naming a segment and then inventing its size or purchase rate; a segment is only as real as the tagged evidence behind it.

included: the US fashion/costume plated-jewelry buyer as unit of analysis
the three decisions segmentation serves (assortment, poll target, ad audience)
every cut framed as a tagged testable hypothesis
excluded: the poll instrument and SKU selection (S4/S5)

pros.claim: Anchoring segmentation to concrete downstream decisions stops it becoming an abstract demographic essay and keeps only actionable cuts
pros.example: the 18-25 gender/occasion cut is kept because it directly sets the poll audience, while a non-actionable cut is dropped

cons.claim: A decision-first frame can prematurely narrow the buyer to the owner's prior before the data is pulled
cons.example: over-committing to '18-25 women' as the unit could hide an older gifting segment the data would show

failure_modes: naming a segment and inventing its size or purchase rate instead of tagging the evidence
framing a cut as a fact rather than a testable hypothesis
acceptance_tests: the unit of analysis, the three decisions segmentation serves, and the rule that every cut is a tagged testable hypothesis are all stated
revisit_triggers: the downstream decision set changes (e.g. a retail channel is added)
the owner redefines the target buyer
kb1 revises the fashion/costume tier definition

base.update_signal: the target buyer or the downstream decision set changes

nodes.definition: Establish the honesty discipline that binds every claim in the KB: [FACT] = a cited public-data or regulatory truth stated with its basis (e.g. a BLS CE table, a Census count, an FTC definition); [ESTIMATE] = a derived number stated with its method and a confidence level; [METHOD] = a recipe for obtaining a number not yet pulled; [UNKNOWN] = an honest gap. No demographic, ethnicity, gender-split or purchase-rate number may appear untagged or as an invented fact [FACT-honesty contract]. This is the direct answer to the owner asking 'how many / which ethnicity / what %': the factory encodes HOW to measure each, or an honest gap, never a guess dressed as data. The protocol also forbids laundering an estimate into a fact by repetition.

included: the four-tag scheme with a basis requirement
the no-untagged-number rule
the ban on laundering estimate into fact
excluded: the anti-stereotyping ethics specific to the ethnic cut (STEREOTYPE_GUARDRAIL)

pros.claim: A fixed tagging scheme makes it structurally impossible to slip an invented market number past review
pros.example: a claimed '40% of Gen Z buys gold-plated' cannot be stated without a [FACT] source, so it is downgraded to a [METHOD] to measure it

cons.claim: Heavy tagging can read as hedging and frustrate a stakeholder who wants one number to act on
cons.example: an owner may want 'the market size' and receive a tagged band plus a method instead

failure_modes: stating a demographic or purchase number without a tag or basis
repeating an [ESTIMATE] until it is treated as a [FACT]
acceptance_tests: the four-tag scheme with the basis requirement and the no-untagged-number rule are stated, with an example of a purchase-rate claim being downgraded to a [METHOD]
revisit_triggers: a new authoritative dataset promotes an [ESTIMATE] to a [FACT]
a reviewer finds an untagged number in an output
the honesty contract is revised upstream

base.update_signal: a dataset promotes an estimate to fact or an untagged number is found

nodes.definition: Catalog the public datasets that feed segmentation and pin what each can and cannot say, with its lag and bias: US Census / ACS / PUMS = population base rates (age x sex x race/ethnicity x income x geography), the denominator, no purchase behaviour, ~1-2yr lag [FACT-scope]; BLS Consumer Expenditure Survey = average annual 'jewelry and watches' expenditure by age-of-reference-person / income quintile, a national probability sample with standard errors, annual, the least-bad purchase proxy [FACT-scope]; platform audience insights (Meta/TikTok ad manager) = reachable-audience size and composition, engagement not purchase, self-selection + platform-composition bias, near-real-time [FACT-scope]; secondary: Google Trends (relative search interest, not counts), industry/trade reports (often paywalled, method-opaque, treat as [UNKNOWN] basis unless method is disclosed). The map is the routing table: each later cut names which dataset supplies it.

included: Census/ACS, BLS CE, platform insights, Trends and trade reports with each scope+lag+bias
the routing of each cut to a dataset
excluded: the deep method of Census (CENSUS_ACS_METHOD) and CE (BLS_CE_METHOD)

pros.claim: A single dataset routing table prevents pulling a purchase number from a source that structurally cannot carry it
pros.example: routing 'how many 18-25 women exist' to Census and 'how much they spend on jewelry' to CE stops anyone reading purchase off Census

cons.claim: Public datasets lag and use coarse categories, so the map cannot supply a fresh or jewelry-specific-enough cut on its own
cons.example: CE's 'jewelry and watches' bundles watches with jewelry and lags a year

failure_modes: treating a paywalled trade report's headline as a [FACT] without a disclosed method
reading purchase behaviour off Census population data
acceptance_tests: Census/ACS, BLS CE and platform insights are cataloged with each one's scope, lag and bias, and each downstream cut is routed to a named dataset
revisit_triggers: a dataset releases a new vintage or changes its category taxonomy
a new usable public dataset appears
a trade report discloses its method and becomes citeable

base.update_signal: a dataset vintage, taxonomy, or availability changes

nodes.definition: Establish Census/ACS/PUMS as the population denominator and how to pull it: ACS 1-year and 5-year tables give counts by age band, sex, race/ethnicity (which the Census collects as separate race and Hispanic-origin questions [FACT]) and household income by geography; PUMS microdata lets you build a custom cross-tab (e.g. women aged 18-25 by household income by metro) that no pre-canned table offers. This node fixes that Census supplies HOW MANY PEOPLE EXIST in a cut and NEVER how many buy - it is the denominator in prevalence x frequency, and using it as a purchase signal is a category error. Geography matters for a DTC brand: national base rates differ from a metro the brand's ads over-index. Every count pulled is a [FACT] with its table/vintage; anything about their buying is left to CE or the poll.

included: ACS tables + PUMS custom cross-tabs for age/sex/race-ethnicity/income counts
Census as denominator only
the geography dimension for a DTC brand
excluded: the sizing formula that multiplies this denominator (PREVALENCE_FREQUENCY_SIZING)

pros.claim: PUMS custom cross-tabs give an exact, citeable population base for any segment the brand cares about
pros.example: women 18-25 in the brand's top ad metros can be counted precisely from PUMS as the sizing denominator

cons.claim: ACS/PUMS lag 1-2 years and race/ethnicity categories are coarse, so the denominator is slightly stale and blunt
cons.example: a fast-growing cohort is undercounted by a 5-year ACS pooled sample

failure_modes: reading Census population share as a purchase rate
mixing race and Hispanic-origin as if they were one mutually-exclusive variable
acceptance_tests: ACS tables and PUMS custom cross-tabs are named as the source of age/sex/race-ethnicity/income counts, with Census fixed as denominator-only and the geography dimension noted
revisit_triggers: a new ACS vintage or a decennial census releases
the brand's target geography shifts
Census revises its race/ethnicity question design

base.update_signal: a new ACS/PUMS vintage or a target-geography change

nodes.definition: Establish the BLS Consumer Expenditure Survey as the anchor purchase-propensity proxy and how to read it honestly: CE reports average annual household expenditure, cross-tabbed by age-of-reference-person, income quintile/decile, and some demographic cuts, from a national probability sample with published standard errors [FACT-BLS CE scope]. Jewelry sits in a bundled line (commonly 'jewelry and watches' within apparel-and-services), so the number includes watches and is per HOUSEHOLD keyed to the REFERENCE PERSON, not per individual buyer - two caveats that must ride with any read [FACT-caveat]. CE gives the least-bad public answer to 'who spends more on jewelry by age/income', but a value read from it is an [ESTIMATE] (with its standard error), never a measured purchase rate for the owner's specific plated-jewelry niche. Use the age and income gradients as SHAPE (who indexes high) more than as absolute levels.

included: CE expenditure cross-tabs by age-of-reference-person and income
the watches-bundled and household/reference-person caveats
reading the gradient as shape not absolute level

pros.claim: CE is a real probability-sample expenditure dataset, so an age/income spending gradient read from it is defensible, not invented
pros.example: a CE table showing jewelry-and-watches spend rising with income gives a citeable propensity gradient for the income cut

cons.claim: The jewelry line is bundled with watches and keyed to the household reference person, so it over- or mis-attributes the individual buyer the brand targets
cons.example: a young woman buying for herself in a household whose reference person is a parent is mis-keyed by CE

failure_modes: reading the bundled 'jewelry and watches' figure as pure jewelry
treating a per-household reference-person average as an individual purchase rate
acceptance_tests: CE is stated as the probability-sample expenditure proxy with the watches-bundled and household/reference-person caveats, and any value read from it is tagged an [ESTIMATE] with its standard error, used as gradient shape
revisit_triggers: BLS releases a new CE vintage or revises the jewelry category
a jewelry-specific expenditure dataset becomes available
the standard error on the relevant cell is found too wide to use

base.update_signal: a new CE vintage or a jewelry-category revision

nodes.definition: Establish how to use Meta/TikTok audience insights as a segmentation PROXY and where the proxy breaks: ad-manager tools estimate reachable-audience SIZE by age band, gender and geography, and organic analytics report the composition of the brand's own followers/engagers [FACT-tool scope]. This is powerful for the owner's paid-poll plan because it measures the actual reachable 18-25 audience, but it measures ENGAGEMENT and REACH, not purchase, and the composition is self-selected and platform-skewed [FACT-scope]. Note the platform-policy limit: detailed targeting by sensitive attributes (including ethnicity) has been restricted, so an ethnic cut cannot simply be bought as an ad audience [FACT-ad policy]. Read audience-size estimates as an [ESTIMATE, platform-biased] input for reach planning, and never as evidence of demand or of a purchase rate.

included: ad-manager reach-size by age/gender/geo
organic follower composition
the engagement-not-purchase and ad-policy-on-sensitive-targeting limits

pros.claim: Platform insights measure the actual reachable audience the owner will buy ads against, grounding the poll plan in real reach numbers
pros.example: the ad-manager estimate of reachable US women 18-25 sets the poll's addressable sample frame

cons.claim: Reach and engagement are not purchase, and the audience is self-selected, so a segment inferred from it over-represents the already-engaged
cons.example: the brand's follower base skews to whoever the last viral post attracted, not the buying market

failure_modes: reading follower composition as the market's composition
assuming an ethnic cut can be bought as an ad audience despite sensitive-attribute targeting limits
acceptance_tests: ad-manager reach-size and organic composition are stated as targeting proxies with the engagement-not-purchase caveat and the ad-policy limit on sensitive-attribute targeting
revisit_triggers: a platform changes its audience-estimate or targeting-policy rules
the brand's follower base shifts materially
a new platform enters the owner's channel mix

base.update_signal: a platform audience-estimate or targeting-policy change

nodes.definition: Establish the pervasive bias that discounts every self-reported and engagement-based input to segmentation: people who follow, engage, answer a poll, or already buy from the store are NOT a random draw of the target market, so any share computed from them is inflated toward whatever that engaged group over-represents [FACT-survey methodology]. This is why a poll that says '80% like earrings' cannot be read as 80% of the market, and why the brand's current customers cannot define the whole addressable segment. The mitigation is not to discard these inputs but to (a) tag them [ESTIMATE, self-selected], (b) triangulate against a representative source (Census/CE), and (c) note the direction and likely magnitude of the skew. This node is the caveat carried by platform insights, the poll, and store data alike.

included: self-selection and platform-composition bias on engagement/poll/store data
the tag-triangulate-note-direction mitigation

pros.claim: Naming the bias direction lets an engaged-audience number still be used, corrected, instead of thrown away or trusted blindly
pros.example: a follower-skewed poll result is kept but discounted toward the Census/CE composition rather than read as the market

cons.claim: The magnitude of the skew is usually itself unknown, so the correction is directional not precise
cons.example: we know followers over-represent the engaged but not by exactly how much

failure_modes: reading a poll or follower share as a population rate
discarding a biased-but-informative input entirely instead of correcting it
acceptance_tests: self-selection/platform bias is stated as inflating whatever the engaged group over-represents, with the tag-triangulate-note-direction mitigation and the example that a poll share is not a market share
revisit_triggers: a representative benchmark becomes available to size the skew
the engagement channel or audience changes
a poll result diverges sharply from the representative source

base.update_signal: a representative benchmark or an engagement-channel change

nodes.definition: Establish the ethics guardrail that binds any cultural/ethnic-market segmentation BEFORE that cut is attempted: (1) the ecological fallacy - a group population base rate or an observed occasion behaviour is never an individual's trait and never a fabricated per-group purchase rate [FACT-method ethics]; (2) the no-invented-rate rule - 'ethnicity X buys Y% more gold' is forbidden unless it is a cited [FACT], otherwise it is at most a [METHOD] to measure or an [UNKNOWN]; (3) the platform/legal limit - ad platforms restrict targeting by sensitive attributes and anti-discrimination norms constrain how a protected class may be targeted [FACT-ad policy]; (4) framing hygiene - segment by OBSERVABLE BEHAVIOUR and occasion (e.g. cultural gifting calendars, wedding traditions) rather than by essentialized traits. This node is a hard gate: the ethnic cut may proceed only within these four bounds.

included: ecological-fallacy, no-invented-rate, ad-policy and behaviour-framing bounds
the guardrail as a hard gate on the ethnic cut
excluded: the ethnic cut's actual data method (ETHNIC_CULTURAL_SEGMENTATION)

pros.claim: A pre-committed guardrail lets a genuinely useful cultural-occasion cut exist without sliding into stereotype or invented rates
pros.example: studying an observable cultural wedding-gifting calendar is allowed while asserting a per-ethnicity purchase percentage is blocked

cons.claim: The guardrail can be over-applied to suppress a legitimate, well-sourced cultural signal out of caution
cons.example: a cited [FACT] about a cultural occasion market might be dropped for fear of appearing to stereotype

failure_modes: stating a per-ethnicity purchase rate without a cited source
reading a group base rate as an individual's trait (ecological fallacy)
acceptance_tests: the four bounds - ecological fallacy, no-invented-rate, ad-policy limit and observable-behaviour framing - are stated as a hard gate the ethnic cut must pass
revisit_triggers: ad-platform sensitive-attribute policy changes
a cited authoritative cultural-market dataset appears
a reviewer flags a stereotype or invented rate in the ethnic cut

base.update_signal: ad-policy change or a stereotype/invented-rate flag

nodes.definition: Segment by age cohort with the owner's Gen Z / 18-25 focus, as a two-step method: (1) SIZE the cohort - pull the 18-25 (or 18-24 ACS band) US population, optionally by sex and metro, from Census/ACS/PUMS as the [FACT] denominator; (2) ESTIMATE propensity - read jewelry-and-watches expenditure by age-of-reference-person from BLS CE, noting that CE's youngest reference-person band understates 18-25 individuals still in a parent's household, so CE UNDERSTATES this cohort's true buying and must be read as gradient shape plus a caveat [ESTIMATE with caveat]. The cohort is the owner's primary hypothesis, but the method keeps it falsifiable: if CE and platform reach both show the spend/engagement concentrated elsewhere, the 18-25 focus is revised. No absolute 'X% of Gen Z buys' is asserted - only the sized denominator and the tagged propensity gradient.

included: sizing the 18-25 population from Census
reading age-propensity from CE with the reference-person understatement caveat
keeping the cohort focus falsifiable

pros.claim: Splitting the cohort into a Census denominator plus a CE propensity keeps the age focus evidence-based and testable
pros.example: if CE shows spend concentrated in 35-54 reference-person households, the 18-25 prior is challenged rather than assumed

cons.claim: CE's reference-person keying systematically undercounts young individuals in family households, biasing the age propensity down
cons.example: a spending 22-year-old living with parents is invisible in CE's youngest own-household band

failure_modes: asserting an absolute 'X% of Gen Z buys' figure
reading CE's reference-person age band as the individual buyer's age without the understatement caveat
acceptance_tests: the 18-25 population is sized from Census as denominator and the age propensity is read from CE with the reference-person understatement caveat, with no absolute purchase percentage asserted
revisit_triggers: a new CE or ACS vintage shifts the age gradient
platform reach data contradicts the 18-25 concentration
a youth-specific expenditure source appears

base.update_signal: a CE/ACS vintage or a platform-reach contradiction of the age focus

nodes.definition: Segment by gender while treating the owner's 'mostly girls, 18-25' as a HYPOTHESIS to test, not a fact to encode. Method: (1) size the male/female 18-25 populations from Census as denominators; (2) look for a gender expenditure signal - CE offers limited gender cross-tabs on jewelry and is weak here, so this leans more on platform audience composition (the brand's engagers by gender) and the owner's store data, both [ESTIMATE, self-selected]; (3) state the skew as a tagged estimate with its evidence, and design the poll to MEASURE it rather than presume it. The cut also flags that 'gifting' flips the buyer's gender (a man buying jewelry as a gift for a woman), so a naive 'women only' targeting can miss a real male gifting sub-segment. No hard gender split percentage is asserted as fact.

included: sizing male/female cohorts from Census
gender signal from platform + store data with CE's weakness noted
the male gifting-buyer flip
excluded: poll design to measure the skew (S4)

pros.claim: Treating the gender skew as a hypothesis surfaces the male gifting-buyer the owner's 'girls only' prior would miss
pros.example: a Valentine's/Mother's-Day male gift-buyer segment is retained for testing instead of excluded by assumption

cons.claim: Public gender-specific jewelry expenditure data is weak, so the skew rests largely on self-selected platform/store data until the poll runs
cons.example: CE cannot cleanly separate jewelry spend by the individual's gender, leaving the estimate soft

failure_modes: hardcoding 'women only' and missing the male gifting sub-segment
asserting a precise gender split as measured fact from self-selected data
acceptance_tests: the gender skew is stated as a tagged hypothesis sized from Census and estimated from platform/store data with CE's weakness noted, and the male gifting-buyer flip is flagged, with no hard split asserted as fact
revisit_triggers: the poll returns a measured gender signal
platform or store gender composition shifts
a gender-resolved jewelry expenditure source appears

base.update_signal: a measured poll gender signal or a composition shift

nodes.definition: Segment by cultural/ethnic market strictly within STEREOTYPE_GUARDRAIL, answering the owner's 'which ethnicity buys' as a METHOD, never an invented rate. Legitimate moves: (1) size cultural-community populations and their geographies from Census race/ethnicity + ancestry data as [FACT] denominators; (2) study OBSERVABLE, documentable cultural OCCASION markets - e.g. wedding and festival gifting traditions where jewelry is customary - as behaviour, cited where a [FACT] source exists, else tagged [METHOD]/[UNKNOWN]; (3) route the actual per-community purchase question to a survey/poll or a cited study, never to a guess. Forbidden: asserting 'community X buys N% more' without a citation, or targeting a protected class in a way ad policy restricts. The honest output is 'here are the sized communities and the observable occasion markets to test', plus explicit [UNKNOWN]s where no cited rate exists.

included: sizing cultural communities from Census
observable cultural-occasion markets as behaviour
routing per-community purchase to a cited study or survey
excluded: generic occasion/gifting not tied to a cultural market (OCCASION_GIFTING_CUT)

pros.claim: Framing culture as sized communities plus observable occasion markets yields a usable, honest cut without a single invented rate
pros.example: a documented cultural wedding-jewelry gifting tradition becomes a testable occasion market, sized by community population

cons.claim: Without a cited per-community purchase study, the actionable purchase rate stays [UNKNOWN] and the cut is directional only
cons.example: we can size a community and name its occasion market but not state how many of them buy plated jewelry

failure_modes: asserting a per-community purchase rate without a citation
essentializing a community by a trait rather than an observable behaviour
acceptance_tests: cultural communities are sized from Census and paired with observable occasion markets, with per-community purchase rates routed to a cited study/survey or left explicit [UNKNOWN], all within the guardrail's four bounds
revisit_triggers: a cited cultural-market or community-expenditure study appears
the guardrail policy changes
a poll adds a cultural-occasion question

base.update_signal: a cited cultural-market study or a guardrail-policy change

nodes.definition: Segment by income to align the buyer with the fashion/costume (accessible-price) tier as a METHOD: (1) pull the household-income distribution for the target cohort from Census/ACS as the [FACT] base; (2) read jewelry-and-watches expenditure by income quintile/decile from BLS CE, which shows spend rising with income while the SHARE of budget behaves differently, as the [ESTIMATE] propensity gradient; (3) map willingness-to-pay bands to the accessible fashion/costume price tier - the strategic point is that plated (vs solid-gold) jewelry serves a mid/low-income and value-seeking buyer for whom accessible price is the draw, so the income cut explains WHY the plated tier exists, not just who buys it. The link to a specific price is a [METHOD] handed to the economics specialist (S6); this KB sets the income shape, never a fixed price point.

included: income distribution from Census
CE jewelry expenditure by income quintile as propensity gradient
willingness-to-pay to accessible-tier mapping as method

pros.claim: The income cut explains why the accessible plated tier has a buyer, grounding the product strategy in an expenditure gradient
pros.example: a CE income gradient plus the accessible price of plated pieces frames the value-seeking buyer the brand serves

cons.claim: Higher absolute jewelry spend concentrates at higher incomes, so an income cut alone could mis-point the brand upmarket away from its plated value proposition
cons.example: reading only absolute CE spend would chase high-income solid-gold buyers, not the plated-tier value buyer

failure_modes: fixing a specific retail price here instead of handing the method to S6
chasing absolute high-income spend and abandoning the accessible plated value position
acceptance_tests: the income distribution is pulled from Census and the CE jewelry-by-income gradient is read as an [ESTIMATE], with willingness-to-pay mapped to the accessible tier as a [METHOD] handed to S6, no fixed price asserted
revisit_triggers: a new CE income cross-tab vintage
the brand's price positioning changes
S6 economics returns a price-band constraint

base.update_signal: a CE income-cross-tab vintage or a price-positioning change

nodes.definition: Segment by buying OCCASION, capturing that the same person buys differently across occasions: self-purchase (treat/impulse/self-gifting) vs gift (Valentine's Day, Mother's Day, winter holidays, weddings, birthdays, graduations, anniversaries). Method: read CE and retail-calendar seasonality for when jewelry expenditure spikes [FACT-seasonality pattern], and separate the GIFTER (often a different demographic and gender than the wearer) from the WEARER. Self-gifting among young women is a widely-observed behaviour and a plausible core motive for accessible plated jewelry, but its share is tagged [ESTIMATE] to test via the poll, not asserted. The occasion cut is decision-critical because it drives the launch/marketing CALENDAR and reframes gender (male gift-buyers) and the assortment (giftable price points, gift packaging). Every seasonal claim is a pattern [FACT] where documented; every share is an [ESTIMATE] to measure.

included: self-purchase vs gift occasions
CE/retail-calendar seasonality
gifter-vs-wearer split and self-gifting as an [ESTIMATE]

pros.claim: The occasion cut turns segmentation into a launch calendar and reveals the gifter as a distinct buyer from the wearer
pros.example: a Valentine's male gift-buyer and a self-gifting young woman are two occasion segments driving different creative

cons.claim: Occasion shares are hard to pull from public data and lean on the poll, so the split stays an [ESTIMATE] until measured
cons.example: the self-purchase vs gift ratio for the brand's niche is unknown until the poll asks

failure_modes: asserting a self-gifting share as fact without the poll
collapsing gifter and wearer into one demographic
acceptance_tests: self-purchase vs gift occasions and the gifter-vs-wearer split are stated with CE/retail-calendar seasonality as pattern [FACT] and any occasion share tagged [ESTIMATE] to test via the poll
revisit_triggers: the poll returns occasion-mix data
a new CE seasonal vintage
the brand's launch calendar changes

base.update_signal: a poll occasion-mix result or a new CE seasonal vintage

nodes.definition: Use the owner's already-running website's first-party data as the strongest-but-smallest segmentation signal, 'mindful of the old stuff': order history, web/app analytics audience (age, gender, geography), and best-seller mix reveal who ACTUALLY bought, which no public dataset can. But it is a small, self-selected sample of whoever the store has reached so far, so it is tagged [ESTIMATE, first-party, self-selected] and must be triangulated against Census/CE rather than treated as the whole market [FACT-bias]. Privacy discipline applies: use aggregated analytics, respect consent, and avoid over-fitting the launch to a legacy customer base that may not represent the target 18-25 buyer. Its unique value is as ground truth on realized purchase; its limit is representativeness and volume.

included: order history, analytics audience and best-seller mix as realized-purchase ground truth
the small/self-selected/privacy caveats
the over-fitting warning

pros.claim: First-party data is the only source of actual realized purchase, anchoring segments in real buyers rather than proxies
pros.example: the store's order-linked analytics show the real age/geo of past buyers as a ground-truth check on the CE gradient

cons.claim: The legacy customer base is small and self-selected, so over-fitting the launch to it can miss the target 18-25 buyer the brand now wants
cons.example: an older legacy buyer mix could wrongly steer the 6-SKU launch away from the intended young cohort

failure_modes: over-fitting the launch to an unrepresentative legacy base
using non-aggregated personal data without consent
acceptance_tests: order/analytics/best-seller data is used as realized-purchase ground truth tagged [ESTIMATE, self-selected], triangulated against Census/CE, with privacy discipline and the over-fitting warning stated
revisit_triggers: the store accumulates materially more orders
the customer base shifts toward the target cohort
a privacy/consent constraint changes

base.update_signal: more store orders or a customer-base shift

nodes.definition: Answer the owner's 'how many people buy' with a bottom-up [METHOD], never a headline guess: buyers = population (Census [FACT] denominator for the segment) x prevalence (share of that population who buy the category, from CE participation, a cited study, or the poll - the softest factor, tagged [ESTIMATE]/[UNKNOWN]); annual demand = buyers x frequency (purchases/yr) x average spend/purchase. Each factor is separately sourced and tagged, and the product is delivered as a BAND with a stated confidence, propagating the widest factor's uncertainty (usually prevalence). This is the honest alternative to citing a trade-report market-size figure of opaque method: a transparent multiplication the owner can audit and refine as the poll and store data sharpen prevalence and frequency. A single point estimate is only ever a [DOWNGRADED] band-centre illustration.

included: the population x prevalence x frequency x spend formula
per-factor sourcing and tagging
the band-with-confidence output and [DOWNGRADED] point rule

pros.claim: A transparent bottom-up multiplication gives an auditable, refinable market size instead of an opaque cited headline
pros.example: sizing = 18-25 women count x tagged prevalence x frequency x spend, each factor visible and updatable from the poll

cons.claim: Prevalence is the softest factor and often [UNKNOWN] until the poll, so the band can be wide
cons.example: with prevalence a factor-of-two unknown, the sizing band spans a wide range until measured

failure_modes: citing a trade-report market-size number of opaque method as fact
collapsing the band to a single point and quoting it as measured
acceptance_tests: the buyers = population x prevalence x frequency x spend method is stated with each factor sourced and tagged, delivered as a band with confidence, and any single point flagged a [DOWNGRADED] band-centre illustration
revisit_triggers: the poll or store data sharpens prevalence or frequency
a cited category-participation study appears
a new CE spend vintage lands

base.update_signal: a poll/store prevalence-frequency sharpening or a new CE vintage

nodes.definition: Combine the individually-imperfect sources into one confidence-weighted segment profile: Census (representative denominator, no purchase), CE (representative expenditure, bundled/reference-person-keyed), platform insights (fresh, self-selected), and first-party store data (real purchase, small/self-selected). Method: where sources AGREE on a segment's shape, raise confidence and tag [ESTIMATE, corroborated]; where they DISAGREE, do not average blindly - flag the divergence, prefer the more representative source for population shares and the first-party source for realized purchase, and mark the residual an [UNKNOWN] for the poll to resolve. The output is a segment profile that is explicit about its evidence per attribute, so no attribute rests on a single fabricated figure. This node is the honest antidote to picking whichever source flatters the owner's prior.

included: confidence-weighted combination of Census/CE/platform/store
agree-raise / disagree-flag rules
per-attribute evidence transparency

pros.claim: Confidence-weighting turns four weak sources into one honest profile that shows where evidence agrees and where it is unknown
pros.example: an age shape corroborated by CE and store data is tagged high-confidence while a gender split they dispute is flagged for the poll

cons.claim: Triangulation cannot manufacture certainty where all sources are weak, so some attributes stay [UNKNOWN]
cons.example: if no source resolves per-community purchase, it remains an explicit gap the profile carries

failure_modes: blindly averaging disagreeing sources into a false consensus
cherry-picking the source that flatters the owner's prior
acceptance_tests: Census/CE/platform/store are combined with agree-raise-confidence and disagree-flag rules, preferring representative sources for shares and first-party for purchase, with residual gaps marked [UNKNOWN]
revisit_triggers: a new source is added or an existing one revised
the poll resolves a previously-divergent attribute
sources newly agree or diverge on a segment

base.update_signal: a new/revised source or a poll-resolved attribute

nodes.definition: Rank the segments for actionability given the owner's DTC / paid-social reality, so the launch and poll focus on what can be served and reached. Method: score each candidate segment on (a) size (Census-sized), (b) propensity (CE/store gradient), (c) reachability (platform audience availability and cost), and (d) fit to the accessible plated tier, then designate a PRIMARY segment (the testable spearhead, likely the 18-25 self-purchasing woman as the owner's prior, pending confirmation) and one or two SECONDARY segments (e.g. the gift-buyer). Non-actionable-but-real segments are noted, not chased. The ranking is explicitly provisional and re-run when the poll returns. This node converts the analytic cuts into a decision the assortment (S5) and poll (S4) specialists can act on, without asserting any segment's size as fact.

included: scoring segments on size/propensity/reachability/tier-fit
designating primary + secondary segments
provisional ranking re-run on poll return

pros.claim: Scoring on reachability and tier-fit, not just size, keeps the launch focused on segments the brand can actually serve and buy ads against
pros.example: a large but unreachable segment is deprioritized below a smaller, cheaply-reachable 18-25 audience

cons.claim: Prioritizing the reachable prior can entrench the owner's assumption before the poll tests it
cons.example: leading with 18-25 women could crowd out a gift-buyer segment the poll might have elevated

failure_modes: locking the primary segment before the poll can challenge it
ranking on size alone and ignoring reachability/cost
acceptance_tests: segments are scored on size, propensity, reachability and tier-fit, a primary and secondary segments are designated as provisional, and the ranking is marked to re-run when the poll returns
revisit_triggers: the poll returns a segment signal
ad reachability or CPMs shift
a secondary segment outperforms the primary in a test

base.update_signal: a poll segment signal or an ad-reachability shift

nodes.definition: Compose the deliverable segment profiles (personas) from the prioritized, triangulated cuts - WITHOUT inventing a single percentage. Each persona states its cuts (age band, gender lean, income tier, occasion motive, any cultural-occasion note) and, crucially, attaches the EVIDENCE TAG per attribute: [FACT] size from Census, [ESTIMATE] propensity from CE/store with confidence, [UNKNOWN] where no source resolves it. A persona is a research summary with its uncertainty visible, not a fabricated 'this customer is 34% of the market' claim. The primary persona (the owner's likely 18-25 self-purchasing woman) and secondary personas (gift-buyer, value-seeker) are written so the poll can validate them and the assortment can weight them. This is the human-readable face of the whole KB and the anti-fabrication discipline is most visible here.

included: per-persona cuts with an evidence tag per attribute
primary + secondary personas written for poll validation
the no-invented-percentage rule made visible

pros.claim: Attaching an evidence tag per attribute makes each persona auditable and blocks the classic fabricated-percentage persona
pros.example: a persona reads 'age 18-25 [FACT-Census sized], self-purchase motive [ESTIMATE, poll-pending]' rather than an invented share

cons.claim: Tagged, uncertainty-visible personas are less punchy than a confident fabricated persona and can underwhelm a stakeholder
cons.example: an owner wanting a crisp 'our customer is X' gets a hedged, sourced profile instead

failure_modes: stating a persona's market share as a fabricated percentage
dropping the per-attribute evidence tags for a cleaner-looking persona
acceptance_tests: each persona states its cuts with an evidence tag per attribute ([FACT] size, [ESTIMATE] propensity, [UNKNOWN] gaps), primary and secondary personas are written for poll validation, and no market-share percentage is fabricated
revisit_triggers: the poll validates or refutes a persona
a new source resolves an [UNKNOWN] attribute
the assortment specialist requests a re-weighting

base.update_signal: a poll validation or a resolved [UNKNOWN] attribute

nodes.definition: Audit the whole segmentation output against the honesty contract before hand-off: enumerate, in one ledger, (a) the [FACT]s with basis (Census counts, CE tables, FTC/ad-policy facts), (b) the [ESTIMATE]s with method + confidence (propensity gradients, sizing bands), and (c) the [UNKNOWN]s (per-community purchase rates, prevalence pending the poll, gender split pending measurement). It explicitly re-flags any single-point number as a [DOWNGRADED] band-centre illustration and confirms no fabricated demographic, ethnicity, gender-split or purchase-rate figure survived into the output. This is the final gate that operationalizes HONESTY_TAGGING_PROTOCOL on the actual deliverable, giving the owner a clear map of what is known, estimated, and genuinely unknown - the direct, honest answer to the questions a factory must not invent.

included: the FACT/ESTIMATE/UNKNOWN ledger over the whole output
re-flagging single points as [DOWNGRADED]
confirming no fabricated figure survived

pros.claim: A final ledger makes the honesty contract auditable on the actual deliverable, not just aspirational
pros.example: a reviewer can scan the ledger and confirm every purchase-rate is a [METHOD] or [UNKNOWN], never an invented figure

cons.claim: The ledger exposes how much is [UNKNOWN], which can read as the analysis being thin
cons.example: a large [UNKNOWN] column pre-poll may disappoint an owner expecting firm numbers

failure_modes: letting a fabricated or untagged number pass the ledger
presenting a [DOWNGRADED] point without its band
acceptance_tests: the ledger enumerates the [FACT]s with basis, [ESTIMATE]s with method+confidence and [UNKNOWN]s, re-flags single points as [DOWNGRADED], and confirms no fabricated demographic/ethnicity/gender/purchase-rate figure survived
revisit_triggers: any output number is added or changed
the poll converts an [UNKNOWN] to an [ESTIMATE]
the honesty contract is revised

base.update_signal: an output number changes or an [UNKNOWN] is resolved

nodes.definition: Compose the clean hand-off from segmentation to the poll (S4) and assortment (S5) specialists, and stop at the scope boundary. To the poll: the TARGET FRAME (which segment(s) to sample, the addressable reachable audience from platform insights, and the specific [UNKNOWN]s the poll must resolve - prevalence, gender split, occasion mix, per-community rates). To the assortment: the prioritized personas with their tagged confidence and the sizing band, so SKU weighting reflects the primary/secondary segments. Explicitly OUT of scope and NOT decided here: the poll instrument wording and incentive/sampling mechanics (S4), and the 6-SKU selection and keep/cut protocol (S5). The hand-off carries the honesty ledger with it so downstream specialists inherit the tags, never a laundered fabricated number.

included: the target frame + [UNKNOWN]s to the poll
the prioritized personas + sizing band to assortment
carrying the honesty ledger across

pros.claim: A scoped hand-off tells the poll exactly which unknowns to resolve and the assortment which segments to weight, without overstepping into their design
pros.example: the poll receives 'measure prevalence and gender split for the 18-25 self-purchaser' rather than a vague 'ask about jewelry'

cons.claim: The hand-off passes a band and open [UNKNOWN]s, so downstream specialists inherit uncertainty they must resolve, not a settled answer
cons.example: the assortment must weight SKUs against a prevalence band the poll has yet to tighten

failure_modes: overstepping into poll instrument or SKU design this KB does not own
handing off a laundered single number instead of the tagged band and ledger
acceptance_tests: the target frame and specific [UNKNOWN]s are handed to the poll, the prioritized tagged personas and sizing band to assortment, the honesty ledger travels with them, and instrument/SKU design is explicitly left out of scope
revisit_triggers: the poll or assortment specialist requests a re-scope
a resolved [UNKNOWN] changes the target frame
the downstream specialist roster changes

base.update_signal: a downstream re-scope request or a resolved [UNKNOWN]

edges.why_related: the small self-selected first-party base and the representative Census denominator can imply different buyer profiles, tempting over-fitting to legacy customers
edges.resolution_rule: use first-party data as ground truth on realized purchase but weight the representative Census/CE sources for population shares; never let the legacy base override the representative denominator when defining the addressable market

edges.why_related: the tagging discipline constrains the sizing to a tagged band, forbidding an untagged headline market-size figure

edges.why_related: poll results returned via the hand-off feed back to re-triangulate the segment profiles

conflict_axes.name: representative_data_vs_fresh_engagement
conflict_axes.description: CE/Census are representative but lagged and coarse, while platform insights and store data are fresh and granular but self-selected; each can be over-trusted.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: use representative sources for population shares and propensity shape, fresh sources for reach and realized purchase, and flag disagreement as an [UNKNOWN] for the poll

conflict_axes.name: owner_prior_vs_falsifiable_test
conflict_axes.description: The owner's '18-25 women, self-purchase' prior is a useful spearhead but can become a self-fulfilling assumption that suppresses a gift-buyer or older segment.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: designate the prior as the provisional primary segment but hold it as a hypothesis the poll must confirm, and keep secondary segments alive

conflict_axes.name: cultural_signal_vs_stereotype_risk
conflict_axes.description: A cultural/ethnic occasion market can be a real, useful segment or a slide into stereotype and invented per-group rates.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: segment only by sized communities and observable occasion behaviour within the four guardrail bounds; leave per-community purchase rates [UNKNOWN] unless cited

conflict_axes.name: wearer_vs_gifter_targeting
conflict_axes.description: The wearer (often a young woman) and the gifter (often a different gender/age) are distinct buyers, so a single-target strategy misses one.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: carry both as occasion-linked sub-segments and let the occasion calendar decide which to weight when

conflict_axes.name: absolute_spend_vs_accessible_tier_fit
conflict_axes.description: Absolute jewelry spend rises with income, which could pull the brand upmarket away from the accessible plated tier its value proposition serves.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: read the CE income gradient as shape but anchor targeting to the value-seeking accessible-tier buyer the plated product actually serves

conflict_axes.name: point_number_vs_honest_band
conflict_axes.description: Stakeholders want a single market-size and single segment-share number, while the evidence supports only tagged bands with wide prevalence uncertainty.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: deliver a band with confidence and label any single point a [DOWNGRADED] band-centre illustration, never a measured figure

conflict_axes.name: reachability_vs_true_size
conflict_axes.description: The largest real segment may be expensive or impossible to reach via paid social, while a smaller segment is cheaply reachable, so size and actionability diverge.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: score both size and reachability/cost and lead the launch with the actionable segment while noting the larger unreachable one

conflict_axes.name: engagement_share_vs_purchase_rate
conflict_axes.description: A poll or follower share reads like a purchase rate but is self-selected engagement, so treating it as demand overstates the market.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: tag every engagement/poll share [ESTIMATE, self-selected], triangulate against a representative source, and never promote it to a population purchase rate

conflict_axes.name: first_party_truth_vs_representativeness
conflict_axes.description: First-party store data is the only realized-purchase truth but is a small, unrepresentative legacy sample, so it is both the most and least trustworthy source.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: use store data as ground truth on WHO bought but not on market shares; triangulate against Census/CE and avoid over-fitting the launch to the legacy base

edge_cases.description: A per-ethnicity purchase rate ('community X buys N% more gold-plated') is stated without a cited source
edge_cases.trigger: the ethnic cut asserts a group purchase percentage not backed by a [FACT] citation
edge_cases.mitigation: downgrade to a [METHOD] to measure it or an explicit [UNKNOWN]; segment only by sized communities and observable occasion behaviour

edge_cases.description: A CE 'jewelry and watches' expenditure figure is read as pure plated-jewelry purchase by the individual 18-25 buyer
edge_cases.trigger: the bundled, household/reference-person-keyed CE line is treated as an individual jewelry purchase rate
edge_cases.mitigation: keep the watches-bundled and reference-person caveats attached and use CE as gradient shape, tagging any level an [ESTIMATE] with its standard error

edge_cases.description: A poll or follower share (e.g. '80% like earrings') is reported as 80% of the market
edge_cases.trigger: a self-selected engagement share is read as a population purchase rate
edge_cases.mitigation: tag it [ESTIMATE, self-selected], triangulate against Census/CE, and state the skew direction rather than reading it as a market rate

edge_cases.description: A trade-report market-size headline of undisclosed method is cited as the market size
edge_cases.trigger: an opaque secondary market-size figure is adopted as a [FACT]
edge_cases.mitigation: replace it with the transparent bottom-up prevalence x frequency band, and only cite the report if its method is disclosed

edge_cases.description: The launch is over-fitted to the legacy customer base, missing the target 18-25 buyer
edge_cases.trigger: first-party store composition is treated as the whole addressable market
edge_cases.mitigation: use store data as realized-purchase ground truth but weight representative Census/CE for shares and keep the target cohort in view

edge_cases.description: The gender skew is hardcoded as 'women only', excluding the male gift-buyer
edge_cases.trigger: the owner's 'mostly girls' prior is encoded as a fact and the gifter is dropped
edge_cases.mitigation: keep the gender skew a tested hypothesis and retain the male gifting sub-segment for occasion-driven targeting

edge_cases.description: A single-point market-size or segment-share is quoted as measured rather than a band-centre illustration
edge_cases.trigger: the sizing band is collapsed to one number and presented as fact
edge_cases.mitigation: carry the band with confidence and label any point a [DOWNGRADED] band-centre illustration

edge_cases.description: Census population share for a cohort is used directly as its purchase rate
edge_cases.trigger: a Census denominator is mistaken for a purchase signal
edge_cases.mitigation: keep Census as denominator only and multiply by a separately-sourced tagged prevalence factor

edge_cases.description: An ethnic segment is attempted as a paid-ad audience despite platform sensitive-attribute targeting restrictions
edge_cases.trigger: the ethnic cut is operationalized as an ad-targeting parameter
edge_cases.mitigation: target observable interests/occasions and geography instead of protected attributes, per ad policy, and keep the cultural cut analytical not a targeting parameter

edge_cases.description: Sources disagree on a segment attribute and are blindly averaged into a false consensus
edge_cases.trigger: triangulation averages divergent sources instead of flagging the divergence
edge_cases.mitigation: prefer the representative source for shares and first-party for realized purchase, and mark the residual an [UNKNOWN] for the poll

edge_cases.description: The primary segment is locked before the poll can challenge it
edge_cases.trigger: prioritization treats the provisional primary as final pre-poll
edge_cases.mitigation: keep the ranking provisional, pass the open [UNKNOWN]s to the poll, and re-run prioritization on poll return

edge_cases.description: A stale ACS/PUMS vintage undercounts a fast-growing cohort used as the sizing denominator
edge_cases.trigger: an old Census vintage is used for a rapidly-changing segment
edge_cases.mitigation: use the latest ACS vintage and note the lag as an uncertainty on the denominator

workflow.description: State the ecological-fallacy, no-invented-rate, ad-policy and observable-behaviour bounds as a hard gate on the ethnic cut
workflow.gate: the four guardrail bounds are stated as a hard gate

workflow.description: Segment by age (18-25 focus), gender (as hypothesis), culture (within guardrail), income and occasion, each sized from Census and estimated from CE/platform/store with tags
workflow.gate: each cut states its Census denominator and tagged propensity source with its caveat

workflow.description: Add the store's realized-purchase data as self-selected ground truth with privacy discipline and the over-fitting warning
workflow.gate: store data is tagged [ESTIMATE, self-selected] with privacy and over-fitting caveats

workflow.description: Compute buyers = population x prevalence x frequency x spend with each factor tagged, delivered as a band with confidence
workflow.gate: the four-factor method is stated with tags and a band-with-confidence output

workflow.action: Triangulate the sources into segment profiles
workflow.description: Combine Census/CE/platform/store with agree-raise and disagree-flag rules into confidence-tagged profiles
workflow.gate: the profiles show per-attribute evidence with divergences flagged [UNKNOWN]

workflow.description: Score segments on size, propensity, reachability and tier-fit and designate provisional primary/secondary segments
workflow.gate: segments are scored on four dimensions with a provisional primary and secondaries

workflow.description: Write primary/secondary personas with an evidence tag per attribute and no fabricated percentage
workflow.gate: each persona has a per-attribute tag and no market-share is fabricated

workflow.description: Run the honesty ledger, then hand the target frame and [UNKNOWN]s to the poll and the tagged personas plus sizing band to assortment, stopping before instrument/SKU design
workflow.gate: the ledger confirms no fabricated figure survived and the scoped hand-off to S4/S5 is stated

dominance_rules.rule: A cited [FACT] source dominates any uncited number
dominance_rules.rationale: the honesty contract forbids asserting a demographic or purchase figure without a basis
dominance_rules.trigger: a segment number is stated without a cited source
dominance_rules.action: downgrade it to an [ESTIMATE] with method, a [METHOD] to measure it, or an [UNKNOWN]

dominance_rules.rule: Representative sources dominate self-selected ones for population shares
dominance_rules.rationale: Census/CE are probability samples while platform/store data are self-selected
dominance_rules.trigger: a population share is drawn from platform or store data
dominance_rules.action: use the representative source for the share and reserve self-selected data for reach and realized-purchase truth

dominance_rules.rule: The anti-stereotyping guardrail dominates any cultural-signal opportunity
dominance_rules.rationale: a useful cultural cut is not worth a stereotype or an invented per-group rate
dominance_rules.trigger: the ethnic cut is tempted to assert a per-community purchase rate
dominance_rules.action: hold the four guardrail bounds and leave the rate [UNKNOWN] unless cited

dominance_rules.rule: Census-as-denominator dominates any attempt to read purchase off it
dominance_rules.trigger: a Census share is used as a purchase rate
dominance_rules.action: keep Census as denominator and multiply by a separately-sourced prevalence

dominance_rules.rule: The honest band dominates any single-point market-size
dominance_rules.rationale: prevalence uncertainty makes a point figure unsupportable
dominance_rules.trigger: a single sizing number is quoted as measured
dominance_rules.action: carry the band with confidence and label the point a [DOWNGRADED] illustration

dominance_rules.rule: A testable hypothesis dominates the owner's prior
dominance_rules.rationale: the frame requires every cut to stay falsifiable
dominance_rules.trigger: the '18-25 women' prior is treated as established fact
dominance_rules.action: hold it as the provisional primary segment and let the poll confirm or refute it

dominance_rules.rule: Reachability plus size dominates size alone in prioritization
dominance_rules.rationale: an unreachable segment cannot be served by the DTC/paid-social model
dominance_rules.trigger: a segment is ranked on size while ignoring reach cost
dominance_rules.action: score reachability and tier-fit alongside size and lead with the actionable segment

dominance_rules.rule: First-party realized purchase dominates proxies for WHO bought, not for shares
dominance_rules.rationale: store data is the only realized-purchase truth but is unrepresentative
dominance_rules.trigger: store composition is used to set market shares
dominance_rules.action: use it for who-bought ground truth and triangulate representative sources for shares

anti_rework_rules.rule: Set the honesty tagging protocol before pulling any number
anti_rework_rules.prevents: an untagged fabricated figure entering the analysis and having to be scrubbed from every downstream artifact

anti_rework_rules.rule: Route each cut to its correct dataset before reading a value
anti_rework_rules.prevents: reading purchase off Census or an individual rate off CE and re-deriving the whole cut later

anti_rework_rules.rule: Apply the anti-stereotyping guardrail before attempting the ethnic cut
anti_rework_rules.prevents: an invented per-community rate or a stereotype that must be retracted and re-framed

anti_rework_rules.rule: Keep the owner's prior a provisional hypothesis from the outset
anti_rework_rules.prevents: locking the launch on '18-25 women' and re-doing segmentation when the poll shows a gift-buyer or older segment

anti_rework_rules.rule: Carry sizing as a tagged band, not a point, from the first computation
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a single number circulating as measured and having to be re-qualified across every deliverable

anti_rework_rules.rule: Attach a per-attribute evidence tag when each persona is first written
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a persona with a fabricated share being handed downstream and later corrected

anti_rework_rules.rule: Triangulate before prioritizing, and flag divergences as [UNKNOWN]
anti_rework_rules.prevents: prioritizing on a single flattering source and re-ranking once the divergence surfaces

anti_rework_rules.rule: Define the S4/S5 scope boundary before hand-off
anti_rework_rules.prevents: over-designing the poll instrument or SKU set here and having the downstream specialist redo it

iteration_protocol.trigger: the IG/TikTok poll returns prevalence, gender or occasion signal
iteration_protocol.action: convert the relevant [UNKNOWN]s to [ESTIMATE]s, re-triangulate and re-run the sizing and prioritization

iteration_protocol.trigger: a new BLS CE or Census/ACS vintage is released
iteration_protocol.action: refresh the denominator and propensity gradients and re-band the affected cuts

iteration_protocol.trigger: the store accumulates materially more first-party orders
iteration_protocol.action: re-weight the first-party signal in triangulation and re-check the personas against realized purchase

iteration_protocol.trigger: a cited cultural-market or per-community expenditure study appears
iteration_protocol.action: promote the relevant ethnic-cut [UNKNOWN] to a tagged [FACT]/[ESTIMATE] within the guardrail

iteration_protocol.trigger: a platform changes its audience-estimate or sensitive-attribute targeting policy
iteration_protocol.action: update the reach proxy and re-check reachability scoring and the ethnic-cut targeting note

iteration_protocol.trigger: the assortment or poll specialist requests a re-scoped hand-off
iteration_protocol.action: revise the target frame and persona weighting passed downstream

priority_rationale: The frame, honesty protocol and dataset map come first because every cut depends on a defined buyer, a tagging discipline and a correct source routing; the Census and CE methods and the anti-stereotyping guardrail are the shared foundations the cuts draw on; the age, gender, cultural, income and occasion cuts plus first-party store data are the core segmentation work, each sized from Census and estimated from a tagged source; prevalence x frequency sizing and triangulation then combine the cuts into confidence-weighted profiles; and prioritization, persona composition, the honesty ledger and the hand-off come last because they turn the analysis into a tagged, auditable deliverable scoped for the poll and assortment specialists.
